title.en: Projection stability review and an unstructured control run

summary: Judge which apparent structure in a projection survives reseeding, and include a control run with unstructured data.
objective: Only structure stable across runs is described as a finding, and a control run is recorded beside the real one.
applies_when: High-dimensional data is displayed through a dimensionality-reducing projection.
The method has a random seed or sensitive parameters.
A viewer may read apparent clusters as categories.
intent_signals: the layout changes completely when I rerun it
example_prompts: Review whether the clusters in this embedding projection are stable.
negative_signals: claiming semantic categories from a layout

principles: A projection is a lossy map, so apparent clusters and distances belong to the projection as much as to the data; the check asks how much of the picture survives a change of parameters.
This review is advisory about being misled rather than aesthetic: it does not declare one layout more beautiful or more correct than another.
Original vectors remain the reference, so a distance readout must name its space and projected coordinates must never overwrite the source data.
implementation: Recompute the projection with at least three seeds where the method is randomized, and with several settings of its main parameter; for a deterministic method reseeding is not independent evidence, so vary initialization, parameters or data subsampling instead and say which was varied.
Ask a specific written question of each pair of runs: do the same points stay grouped, and does any apparent gap between groups persist across all runs.

Run a control by projecting a dataset drawn from a specified distribution with no group structure, recording its sample size, dimension, normalization and the identical method parameters, and note whether that result also looks clustered.
Verify in the data that projected coordinates are stored separately from the original vectors and that every distance readout names its space.
observable_checks: Structure appearing in only some runs is reported as unstable and is not described in the artifact as a finding.

The control run is recorded beside the real one with its distribution, sample size, dimension and normalization stated, so a reader can see how much apparent grouping the method produces on data with no groups.
Original vectors are unchanged after projection, and every distance readout states whether it belongs to the original or the projected space.

known_limits: A stability and over-reading review; it cannot establish that stable structure is semantically meaningful, and judgments here are advisory rather than a universal standard.
Authored verification guidance; no projection was computed or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: t-SNE visualizes high-dimensional data by giving each data point a location in a two- or three-dimensional map, aiming to reveal structure at many different scales in a single map.
claims.scope: The stated purpose of the technique in the cited paper abstract; it is not a guarantee that distances or cluster separations in the map reproduce those in the original space.
